correctness.rationale: The leaf differences satisfy an exact exponential law, preserving all weighted leaf ranks and forcing the weighted-median endpoints to obey the same hub-driven linear equation. The hub tie-selection is the projection of its current opinion onto the leaf median interval because the hub is an eligible zero-weight candidate. The three sign-invariant linear ODE cases produce the stated formulas and show global consensus for every finite leaf number and every strictly positive weight vector. Exact rational thresholds and independent differential equation residuals were checked with verify.py; the proof is analytic.

value.rationale: The star is the natural hub-and-spoke test graph for social influence and admits arbitrary positively weighted leaves. The theorem gives a complete and explicit basin-to-consensus selection map for this entire topology, stronger than generic convergence. The half-weight phase boundary demonstrates an order-one jump from infinitesimal influence perturbation without support changes; this is directly relevant to robust interpretation of socially weighted consensus and is neither a mere numerical recomputation nor a parameter renaming.
